newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PLAYING FOR BRAZIL COMES FIRST, SAYS JUNINHO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLAYING FOR BRAZIL COMES FIRST, SAYS JUNINHO.

text.p: Juninho has hinted strongly that Saturday's English F.A. Cup final against Chelsea at Wembley will be his last game for premier league Middlesbrough.
Brazil coach Mario Zagallo has said he would only consider players with leading clubs when he assembled his squad for next year's World Cup and Juninho is desperate not to miss out.

"I have to think of my career and see what is best for me," he said on Wednesday. "What's most important for me is to be in the Brazil squad. And to be in the Brazil squad you have to play in good teams.
"Nobody likes playing in the first division."
Manchester United and Atletico Madrid are among the clubs understood to be interested in signing Juninho, who joined Middlesbrough for 4.75 million pounds ($7.6 million) from Sao Paulo in 1995.
But Juninho categorically denied he had already agreed to join Atletico . "That's not true,'' he said.

The Brazilian, who insists he has still not decided his future and will not consider it until after the cup final, said: "Europe's very important. I came here to play in European competition. I'm not just here to play in the league games.
"But I have to talk with Bryan Robson (Middlesbrough's manager) and talk with the chairman before I make a final decision."
Middlesbrough's other expensive foreign buys, Emerson and Fabrizio Ravanelli, did not take part in training on Wednesday.
Emerson has been carrying a knee injury for the past two months but Robson said: "He should be okay for the final."

Ravanelli, Middlesbrough's leading scorer who missed his side's final two premier league games with a wrenched back muscle, is more doubtful. Robson said he would wait until Friday for a verdict on his fitness.
